result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.minimum_spanning_arborescence()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a minimum-weight spanning arborescence of a directed graph (Edmonds' algorithm). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46908-L46976){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.minimum_spanning_arborescence(weight_attr=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Minimum spanning arborescence](/assets/graphs/minimum-spanning-arborescence.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="One-way links between four relay stations, weighted by cost: A→B (4), A→C (1), C→B (2), B→D (3), C→D (6), and D→C (1). The cheapest tree reaching every station from the root A, outlined in the accent color, uses A→C, C→B, and B→D, in the accent color; the other links are faded. The card lists the three edges and their total cost 1 + 2 + 3 = 6." width="100%"} A spanning arborescence is a directed tree in which a single root reaches every node: the root has no incoming edge and every other node has exactly one. This method returns the cheapest one over every possible root. It is the directed counterpart of the minimum spanning tree, and answers questions like "what is the cheapest way to broadcast from one site to all others over one-way links?". Edge direction matters: an edge `u -> v` can only carry the signal from `u` to `v`. Self-loops are never chosen, and the original graph is not modified. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute holding the weights. If `None` (the default), each edge's weight field is used (`1.0` on an unweighted graph). Edges that lack the attribute, or hold a non-numeric value, count as `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new directed graph with every node of the original (IDs, labels and attributes kept) and the `n - 1` arborescence edges (weights and attributes copied). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, an edge value is NaN, or no spanning arborescence exists (no single node can reach all the others). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} This is the Chu-Liu/Edmonds algorithm: Edmonds' cycle contraction on the negated weights, with the edge count ranked first so that every node gets a parent except the root (see `maximum_spanning_arborescence()`). It runs in $O(V E)$ time. Ties between equally cheap arborescences may be broken differently than in NetworkX. ## Examples {.doc-examples} One-way links between four relay stations, weighted by cost. The cheapest way to reach every station starts at A, the only station with no incoming link: ::: {#d0894bb7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) g.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges( [ ("A", "B", 4.0), ("A", "C", 1.0), ("C", "B", 2.0), ("B", "D", 3.0), ("C", "D", 6.0), ("D", "C", 1.0), ] ) tree = g.minimum_spanning_arborescence() tree.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['A->C', 'C->B', 'B->D'] ``` ::: ::: The total cost is 1 + 2 + 3 = 6, cheaper than any tree using the direct edge A -> B: ::: {#c3e79f77 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sum(tree.get_edge(e).weight for e in tree.get_edge_ids(limit=None)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 6.0 ``` ::: :::
